conventions.convention: Total variation is the supremum of absolute event-probability differences, equivalently the supremum over measurable tests taking values in [0,1]. The coupling bound uses a specified measurable agreement event; measurability of the diagonal is unnecessary.

Phi-irreducibility is defined on a countably generated measurable space, relative to a nonzero sigma-finite measure, and requires positive probability of reaching each phi-positive set at some positive integer time from every state.
Small-set minorization holds pointwise for every state in the set and every measurable event, at one fixed integer time m ≥ 1, with a probability minorizer and 0 < epsilon ≤ 1.

An ordinary geometric drift function is measurable, everywhere finite and at least one. An extended certificate may take infinity but must be finite pi-almost everywhere and satisfy the drift inequality pointwise in the extended reals.
A petite minorization uses one common probability distribution over positive integer times; time zero is excluded.
Aperiodicity excludes every positive-pi-mass measurable cyclic family with pointwise deterministic transitions to its successor; the cyclic family need not cover the state space.
Harris recurrence is relative to the specified irreducibility measure and means almost-sure hitting from every state, with hitting times starting at time zero.
The bivariate coupling time records successful splitting with a measurable flag; it does not test equality before success. Epsilon = 1 has no residual branch.

load_bearing.statement: For probability laws on the same measurable space, total variation equals the supremum over measurable [0,1]-valued tests and contracts under a probability kernel. For a coupling and a measurable event E on which its coordinates agree, total variation is at most Pr(E complement).

A phi-irreducible probability kernel on a countably generated space, with nonzero sigma-finite irreducibility measure phi, has an m-small measurable set C with phi(C) > 0 and a probability minorizer nu satisfying nu(C) > 0.

Let P be phi-irreducible and aperiodic with invariant probability pi, and let nu be a probability absolutely continuous with respect to pi. If every state admits a positive-time positive minorization into nu, then for every sufficiently large n, nu P^n dominates a positive multiple of nu.

On a countably generated space, a probability kernel has a jointly measurable density component relative to any nonzero sigma-finite reference measure and a subprobability residual kernel singular to that measure at each source state.

If P has invariant probability pi and a measurable set has positive hitting probability from every state, it is hit almost surely from pi-almost every state. If P is phi-irreducible and phi(A) > 0, then pi(A) > 0 and the positive-hitting premise holds.

Under countable generation, phi-irreducibility, aperiodicity, invariance and geometric drift toward a phi-positive small set, a bounded-V phi-positive small subset supports an improved drift inequality. A skeleton also admits a bounded-V small set, contracting bivariate drift off its square, and bounded residual bivariate expectations.

A one-step small set, a finite measurable h ≥ 1 contracting under the independent product kernel off the set's square, and the stated finite residual expectation bound yield a measurable split-success coupling time with Pr(T > n) ≤ M h(x,y) r^n for some M < infinity and 0 < r < 1.

A countably generated, phi-irreducible, aperiodic kernel with invariant probability pi converges to pi in total variation from pi-almost every state. Harris recurrence relative to phi upgrades convergence to every starting state.

For a countably generated, phi-irreducible, aperiodic kernel with invariant probability pi, geometric drift with finite V ≥ 1 toward a phi-positive small set gives a bound M V(x) r^n for every state and n ≥ 0. For an extended certificate finite pi-almost everywhere, the bound holds on the full-pi absorbing set {V < infinity}.

seams_checked.note: The companion Gibbs example supplies the exact point-mass full conditionals on the finite product space and uses the half-weight random scan. The block-update, scan and invariance interfaces support its invariance claim and make no irreducibility or convergence promise.

Checked the cited irreducibility, aperiodicity, Harris recurrence, small-set definition and positive-measure small-set interfaces. The envelope and split-tour consumers derive the required irreducibility before applying the small-set supplier. The sufficient-regimes theorem assumes its additional stationary, moment and rate hypotheses; it does not infer a CLT from qualitative convergence. Its former direct general-convergence edge is recorded as removed.

The block comparison uses precisely [0,1]-test duality; the convergence theorem uses fixed-kernel contraction and invariance. The uniform drift argument uses pointwise minorization and finite drift, explicitly adding nu_gamma(C) = 1 and common numerical bounds. Its coupling uses a measurable success flag, consistent with the supplier's agreement-event formulation.
